title: How would you estimate how many hotel rooms there are in Paris?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many hotel rooms are there in Paris?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A harder one: you work backwards from guest nights to rooms, dividing by occupancy and guests per room. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many hotel rooms are there in Paris?

The approach

Guest nights per year ÷ 365 ÷ share of rooms filled ÷ guests per room.

Tip: Keep your page tidy: one line per step, the running total circled at the end.

Step by step

  1. Hotel guest nights in Paris per year: 50M
  2. ÷ 365 days in a year
  3. ÷ 75% rooms filled on an average night
  4. ÷ 1.6 guests per room

That gives about 114k rooms.

Does it make sense?

Around 115,000 rooms. Short-term rentals take some visitors who would otherwise stay in hotels.
